composition.rule: Components join with a vertical bar in the order the composition lists them, behind the scheme version. No component may be empty or contain a vertical bar. Every component is the source's own text, unaltered: nothing is hashed, truncated, normalized, or re-encoded.
composition.versioning: The prefix versions this guide's composition rule, not the platform's data. A platform that changes what one of its identifiers means is a new naming system, not a new prefix.
composition.passThrough: An identifier carried through from the platform unchanged takes no prefix, because it composes nothing. Only the compositions below are prefixed.
composition.whyComposedHere: Health Connect's Metadata.id is unique only within one repository on one device, so the raw value cannot identify a record on its own: two participants' phones can both hold the same id for unrelated records. The scope is joined into the value rather than carried in a sibling field because a receiver deduplicates on the complete system and value pair, and a sibling field takes no part in that comparison. Every other Health Connect identifier passes its source value through.

measuredValuesExcluded: No composition takes a measured value as a component. A corrected reading at the same instant keeps its output identifier, so a receiver sees one measurement revised rather than two measurements recorded.

deploymentOwnedIdentities.rule: The conversion Provenance and the exchange Bundle are created by the export, not read from the platform, so they are identified in the deployment's own namespace rather than a namespace this guide owns. Two deployments converting the same Record agree on every identifier above and are expected to differ on these.
deploymentOwnedIdentities.granularity: One export event covers many Records, so these are keyed by the event rather than by a Record. The per-Record roles a deployment also mints, such as a derived recording Device, take <repositoryScope>|<recordTypeToken>|<rawRecordId>|<role>.

lexicalRules.rawRecordId: a non-empty Unicode scalar string exactly as supplied by Health Connect
lexicalRules.writerPackageName: the writing application's Android package name, exactly as supplied by Health Connect
lexicalRules.clientRecordId: a non-empty Unicode scalar string exactly as the writing application supplied it
lexicalRules.sampleInstantUtc9: UTC FHIR instant YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnnZ with exactly nine fractional digits
lexicalRules.startInstantUtc9: UTC FHIR instant YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnnZ with exactly nine fractional digits
lexicalRules.endInstantUtc9: UTC FHIR instant YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnnZ with exactly nine fractional digits
lexicalRules.sourceStageToken: an exact sleep-stage token from catalog/health-connect-adapter.json
lexicalRules.sourceSpecimenToken: an exact specimen token from catalog/health-connect-adapter.json
lexicalRules.occurrenceUnsignedDecimal: 0 or a non-zero ASCII digit followed by zero or more ASCII digits; no sign or leading zero
lexicalRules.eventSequence: a non-zero ASCII digit followed by zero or more ASCII digits; no sign or leading zero
lexicalRules.noSeparatorInComponents: No component may contain U+007C VERTICAL LINE. A source value carrying one is rejected rather than escaped.

r4ResourcePlacement.conversion: Grove exchange entry identifier for the Provenance entry; Provenance has no native identifier in R4
r4ResourcePlacement.androidPackage: Device.identifier for the source or converting application
r4ResourcePlacement.resourceId: optional repository-assigned logical id; never populated from these source or conversion identifiers

vectors.note: Minted in the deployment's own graph namespace, so it carries no scheme-version prefix from this guide.
A raw record id containing a vertical bar is rejected. It is never escaped, because an escaping rule is the conformance surface this scheme exists to remove.

outputIdentity.appliesWhen: Only where one Record yields more than one Observation, such as a HeartRateRecord's samples or a SleepSessionRecord's stages.
outputIdentity.oneToOne: A one-to-one conversion carries the record identifier alone. A second namespace repeating the same value identifies nothing new.
